title: Relative section cone, supports, and change of topology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:W=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on either small site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ or $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. An abelian sheaf means a contravariant functor to abelian groups satisfying the sheaf equalizer condition for covering families. For an abelian sheaf $F$ and a nonnegative injective resolution $F	o I^ ullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], put $A^q=I^q(T)$, $B^q=I^q(W)$, $r=\operatorname{res}:A^ ullet	o B^ ullet$, and $K^ ullet=\ker r$. Extend section complexes by zero in negative degrees. Form the relative section complex $C^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$ with $D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db)$, the signed model of $\operatorname{Cone}(r)[-1]$ [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $A^ ullet$ and $B^ ullet$ compute derived sections on $T$ and $W$, and the inclusion $K^ ullet	o C^ ullet$, $k\mapsto(k,0)$, is a quasi-isomorphism. It canonically identifies relative cohomology $H^q(C^ ullet)$ with $R^q\Gamma_Z(T,F)$, where $\Gamma_Z(T,F)=\ker(F(T)	o F(W))$, the support convention of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Under this identification the projection $C^ ullet	o A^ ullet$ is forgetting support and the localization boundary is represented by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. These comparisons are independent of resolutions and commute with coefficient morphisms, restriction along etale neighbourhoods, and inclusions $W'\subseteq W$ (enlargement of support). Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For any abelian etale sheaf $F$, the canonical derived-section pullbacks on $T$ and $W$ induce an isomorphism $H^q(T,W;F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T_{\mathrm{proet}},W_{\mathrm{proet}};
u_T^{-1}F)$ for every $q\geq0$, commuting with forgetting support, localization boundary, coefficient morphisms, etale restriction and enlargement of support. Here the pro-etale relative group uses the identical signed section-cone construction. For a pro-etale coefficient morphism $
u_T^{-1}F	o F'$, composition gives the same compatibilities with the supported class in $R^q\Gamma_Z(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F')$.

proof.text: Fix the chosen site and the injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$. For every degree $q$, the map $I^q(T)\to I^q(W)$ is restriction along the monomorphism $W\to T$ in the site, hence is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-mono-restriction]. Its kernel is $K^q$, and the differentials preserve these kernels, so $0\to K^\bullet\to A^\bullet\xrightarrow{r}B^\bullet\to0$ is a short exact sequence of complexes. The injective-resolution convention computes the derived sections on both $T$ and $W$ from $A^\bullet$ and $B^\bullet$.

source.place: Section \ref{section-cohomology-support}, second paragraph (restriction $\mathcal I(X)\to\mathcal I(U)$ surjective with kernel $\Gamma_Z(X,\mathcal I)$), citing sites-cohomology.tex Lemma \ref{lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective}

proof.text: Use the signed cone convention of [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. In degree $q$, $C^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$ and $D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db)$. A cycle $(a,b)$ can be changed by the boundary $D(x,0)=(dx,r(x))$: choose $x$ with $r(x)=b$ and replace it by $(a-dx,0)$; the new first component lies in $K^q$. The same calculation for boundaries shows that two elements of $K^q$ become homologous in $C^\bullet$ exactly when they were homologous in $K^\bullet$. Thus $K^\bullet\to C^\bullet$, $k\mapsto(k,0)$, is a quasi-isomorphism in the sense of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Section 13.11 (cone complexes and quasi-isomorphisms), with the displayed degreewise calculation

proof.text: By [def-pur-support-cohomology], the underived supported-sections functor is $\Gamma_Z(T,-)=\ker((-)(T)\to(-)(W))$, and its right derived functors are computed on $I^\bullet$ by the cohomology of this kernel complex. Therefore the quasi-isomorphism of Step 2 canonically identifies $H^q(C^\bullet)$ with $R^q\Gamma_Z(T,F)$. The first cone projection is the map forgetting support, while the cone triangle convention gives the connecting representative $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. All these maps are functorial in coefficient morphisms and in commuting restriction squares, so etale restriction and $W'\subseteq W$ give the stated enlargement-of-support compatibilities. Independence of the resolution: for a second nonnegative injective resolution $F\to I'^\bullet$, a chain map $\varphi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ over $\mathrm{id}_F$ is built inductively from the injectivity of the $I'^n$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Being a morphism of sheaves, it commutes with restriction, so $(a,b)\mapsto(\varphi a,\varphi b)$ maps $K^\bullet$, $C^\bullet$, the inclusion $K^\bullet\to C^\bullet$, the projection to $A^\bullet$ and the boundary $b\mapsto(0,-b)$ to the primed ones. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] with $h=\mathrm{id}_F$, applied to $\Gamma_Z(T,-)$, to $\Gamma(T,-)$ and to $\Gamma(W,-)$, the maps induced on $H^q(K^\bullet)$, $H^q(A^\bullet)$ and $H^q(B^\bullet)$ are the canonical identifications of the derived groups. A second such $\varphi$ differs by $dH+Hd$; then $(a,b)\mapsto(Ha,-Hb)$ satisfies $DH_C+H_CD=(dH+Hd,dH+Hd)$ on $C^\bullet$, since $H$ commutes with $r$. Hence the identification of $H^q(C^\bullet)$ with $R^q\Gamma_Z(T,F)$ does not depend on the resolution.

proof.text:
Write $u_T:T_{\mathrm{et}}	o T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ for the inclusion defining $
u_T$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], so $u_T(T)=T$ and $u_T(W)=W$, and put $L=
u_T^{-1}$, $G=
u_{T,*}$ on abelian sheaves. Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $LF	o J^ ullet$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and, since $L$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], one chain map $ eta:LI^ ullet	o J^ ullet$ under $LF$. For an object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] defines the canonical pullback $
u_T^*:H^p(V,F)	o H^p(V,LF)$ as $H^p$ of $\phi_V:I^ ullet(V)\xrightarrow{\eta}(LI^ ullet)(V)\xrightarrow{ eta}J^ ullet(V)$, independent of the choices. Here $H^p(V,-)$ is the derived functor of sections over the object $V$ of the site of $T$; $A^ ullet$, $B^ ullet$ and $A'^ ullet=J^ ullet(T)$, $B'^ ullet=J^ ullet(W)$ compute these groups. Since $\eta$ and $ eta$ are morphisms of sheaves, $\phi_W\circ r=r'\circ\phi_T$. For $V=T$ the map $H^p(\phi_T)$ is the canonical pullback of [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison], hence an isomorphism. For $V=W$ the argument is made at the object $W$ of the sites of $T$, without identifying these groups with cohomology of the small sites of the scheme $W$. By [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections], the unit $\eta_E:E	o GLE$ is bijective on sections over every etale object for every etale sheaf $E$. The abelian unit has this underlying map [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), so $\eta_F$ and each $\eta_{I^n}$ are isomorphisms of abelian sheaves. Exactness of $L$ makes $LF	o LI^ ullet$ a resolution, and each $LI^n$ is $G$-acyclic by [lem-cbc-abelian-comparison-injective-acyclicity]. By [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (2), $R^qG(LF)=H^q(GLI^ ullet)\cong H^q(I^ ullet)=0$ for $q>0$, using the isomorphism $\eta_{I^ ullet}$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-site-leray-degenerate], for $
u_T$, the sheaf $LF$ and the object $W$, makes $e^p_{W,LF}=H^p(W,\varepsilon_{LF})\circ
u_T^*$ an isomorphism. Coefficient naturality (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] for $\eta_F$ and the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{LF}\circ L\eta_F=\mathrm{id}$ give $e^p_{W,LF}\circ H^p(W,\eta_F)=
u_T^*$ on $H^p(W,F)$. Both factors are isomorphisms, so $H^p(\phi_W)$ is an isomorphism for every $p\ge0$.

proof.text: By Step 4, $(a,b)\mapsto(\phi_Ta,\phi_Wb)$ is a chain map $C^\bullet\to C'^\bullet$ of the signed cones, where $C'$ uses the identical construction on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. It is compatible with the degreewise split short exact sequences $0\to B^{\bullet-1}\to C^\bullet\to A^\bullet\to0$ given by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$ and $(a,b)\mapsto a$, and with their primed versions. [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] give a morphism of long exact sequences $H^{q-1}(A)\to H^{q-1}(B)\to H^q(C)\to H^q(A)\to H^q(B)$ to the primed one. The four outer maps are isomorphisms by Step 4, so the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] shows that $H^q(T,W;F)\to H^q(T_{\mathrm{proet}},W_{\mathrm{proet}};LF)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$. The cone map commutes with forgetting support (projection to $A$) and with the boundary $b\mapsto(0,-b)$ by construction. For etale restriction to $U\to T$ and for $W'\subseteq W$, the same sheaf maps $\eta,\beta$ are evaluated at the other objects, so the squares commute strictly. For a coefficient morphism $\alpha:F\to F_1$, choose lifts $\tilde\alpha:I\to I_1$ and $\tilde\alpha':J\to J_1$ of $\alpha$ and $L\alpha$. The two chain maps $\beta_1\circ L\tilde\alpha$ and $\tilde\alpha'\circ\beta$ both lift $L\alpha$ into the injective resolution $J_1$, so they differ by a homotopy $H$. As in Step 3, $(a,b)\mapsto(Ha,-Hb)$ is a homotopy on the cones, which gives the coefficient compatibility in cohomology. For a pro-etale coefficient morphism $LF\to F'$, the pro-etale cone construction of Steps 1-3 is functorial in the same way, and postcomposition gives the final assertion.

lean.statement: theorem relativeConeSupportComparison (T : Scheme.{u}) {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i] (F : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (I : InjectiveResolution F) : ∃ (E : RelativeCone.System T.smallEtaleTopology (fun {_ _} f ↦ IsOpenImmersion f.left)) (P : RelativeCone.System (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (fun {V _} f ↦ IsOpenImmersion f.left ∧ Etale V.hom)) (e : ∀ q : ℕ, relativeCohomology T (Scheme.Etale.mk i.openComplement.ι) I q ≅ supportCohomology i q F), Nonempty (RelativeCone.TopologyComparison T E P) ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, (e q).hom = ((E.realization (supportRestrictionArrow i) (by change IsOpenImmersion i.openComplement.ι; infer_instance) I).e q).hom
